model: Lender FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, equity retention on balance-sheet growth, SBC expensed

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E total revenues, RMB m: H1 FY2026 actual 6,177 (+13% YoY, interim line 955) + H2 FY2026E ~6,575 (H2 FY2025 actual 11,560 - 5,452 = 6,108, x ~1.08: SaaS +60% and guarantee +22% in H1 against loan facilitation -48% and a China passenger-vehicle market -4.4%; H2 growth is taken below H1's 13% for the regulatory take-rate pressure the analysis flags). FY2025 actual 11,560 (+17%), FY2024 9,888 (+48%), FY2023 6,686.
inputs.share_count_basis: 6,805.2m shares in issue at 30 Jun 2026 (interim line 2063; no treasury shares held, line 3099) plus 148.3m restricted shares and options with potential dilutive effect (interim EPS note line 4463) = 6,953.5m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC (RMB90m H1 FY2026, 144m FY2025) is expensed in the flows, so charging dilution as well would double-count. Weighted average basic count was 6,765m for H1 FY2026 and 6,694m for H1 FY2025; share repurchases are small (RMB12m FY2025, nil H1 FY2026) and no non-SBC issuance is in prospect.
inputs.debt_cash_note: Lender convention: total borrowings RMB32,373m at 30 Jun 2026 (31,280m at FY2025; ABS, syndicated loans, bank facilities, USD bond, green MTNs) fund the RMB32,459m net finance receivables of the self-operated financing-lease book almost 1:1 and are operating funding, not acquisition debt. Cash and restricted cash (RMB4,683m) is liquidity behind the book and the RMB2,870m risk-assurance liabilities on RMB86bn of off-balance-sheet facilitated loans, not surplus. Net debt is therefore zero by construction on the FCFE route and nothing is bridged after the flows; the debt is charged through the cost of funds inside the pre-tax margin and through the equity-retention line. Reported figures retained for the reader: borrowings 32,372.6, cash 4,682.6, lease liabilities ~49 (RMB m, 2026-06-30).
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is FY2026E FCFE, not reported OCF - capex. FY2026E: revenue 12,750 x 15.0% pre-SBC pre-tax margin = 1,912; less SBC ~180 (1.4%) = PBT ~1,732 (H1 actual 847 after RMB87m equity-method losses and a 61% rise in credit impairment); less income tax at ~22% blended (H1 actual 17.0% on the Hainan 15% preferential rate and one-off deductions; FY2025 30.0%) = net profit ~1,350-1,400 (H1 actual 704); less equity retained to hold equity/assets at ~30% on ~3% FY2026 asset growth (0.30 x ~1,700 = ~500) = FCFE ~870. Reported FCF (OCF - capex) is loan-book flow noise: -841 (FY2025), -2,243 (FY2024), -8,682 (FY2023), +12,230 (FY2020) and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 annual report cash-flow add-back and adjusted-net-profit reconciliation: share-based compensation RMB143.7m (1.24% of revenue); H1 FY2026 RMB90.1m at operating level / 83.2m net (interim lines 885, 903), 1.46% of H1 revenue. No cash tax on net-share settlement is disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0 in the Metrics CSV). SBC is projected as a % of revenue and deducted inside the engine so the street basis (SBC added back) equals the company's own 'adjusted net profit' convention.
inputs.interest_income_note: Finance income (RMB73m FY2025, 43m H1 FY2026) stays inside the pre-tax margin because its source asset, the cash pile, is NOT added back in a bridge (net debt zero): the matching-asset rule is satisfied with the income kept and the asset excluded.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts CNY (model; the Group reports in RMB) to HKD (HKEX quote): CNYHKD=X 1.1750 at 2026-10-22T05:42Z, Yahoo Finance chart API. Triangulated the same minute from the same source: USDHKD=X 7.8451 / USDCNY=X 6.6737 = 1.1755 (0.04% apart). Single listing, so no dual-listing parity check is available; direction check: FY2025 final + special dividend HK14.0 cents x 6,787m shares = HK$878.5m per the annual report (line 1358) = ~RMB 800m, consistent with the RMB814m of dividends paid in FY2025 for the prior year's HK13.0 cents. Per-share values are computed in RMB and converted at fx_rate; the unsuffixed intrinsic values are HKD.
inputs.fy0: FY2026E (year ending 2026-12-31, unreported: H1 FY2026 actual + H2 estimate)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-22T05:27:08Z HKEX regular session (13:27 HKT, intraday print; the stock is at its 52-week low of 0.75 against a 52-week high of 3.20, down ~73% from HK$2.85 at end-December 2025, with a 100m-share volume spike on 13-15 Oct 2026). No filing in Extracted/ (latest: interim report, Aug 2026) and no headline reachable from this environment explains the drawdown; it is treated as evidence for the bear weight, not as a known event.
inputs.capital_anchor: Total equity RMB16,788m on total assets RMB54,963m at 30 Jun 2026 = 30.5% (FY2025: 16,954 / 54,361 = 31.2%; FY2024: 16,480 / 48,591 = 33.9%). Debt-to-equity 1.93x (1.85x FY2025, interim line 1823); gearing (net debt / total capital) 59%. Net finance receivables 32,459 (32,600 at FY2025; 31,452 FY2024 per the KPI line, which excludes a reclassification), provision 3.58%, 90+ day past-due 1.92% (1.89% FY2025, 1.86% FY2024). Off-balance-sheet facilitated loans under risk assurance ~RMB86bn (86,367 at FY2025) with risk-assurance liabilities 2,870. BVPS RMB2.41 = HK$2.84; at the current price the stock trades at ~0.27x book and ~3.3x FY2026E earnings.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Single CNY cost of equity 12.0% in every scenario (risk charged once, through the scenario weights, never through per-scenario discount rates). Built in the flows' own currency: 10-year China Government Bond ~1.8% (assumption; the 10Y CGB has traded ~1.6-2.0% since 2025) + beta ~1.2 x China ERP ~6.5% = ~9.6%, plus ~2.4pt for what the index ERP does not price in an H-share minority position in a Tencent-controlled (~52%) non-bank auto lender: wholesale-only funding (no deposits) against a 1.93x debt-to-equity book, retained credit risk on RMB86bn of guaranteed off-balance-sheet loans, a 2025-26 regulatory campaign against high-interest/high-rebate auto lending, and a free float of ~HK$2.5bn. That is 0.5-1.5pt above the house Chinese-bank precedents (0998.HK 10.5%, 2016.HK 11.0%, 1788.HK 11.5% HKD broker). Hurdle for the entry price is the house 15%.
inputs.lease_treatment: IFRS 16 right-of-use depreciation and lease interest (lease liabilities ~RMB49m, immaterial) sit inside operating expenses and so inside the pre-tax margin; lease_cost_pct_path is zero so the charge is not taken twice and nothing is deducted as debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are RMB0.1m (interim line 6714); profit attributable to owners 703,584 vs profit for the period 703,632. Ignored (charged once, inside the cash_tax_rate deduction at zero cost).
inputs.notes: MODEL: lender FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine (dcf-methods routing row 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift' adapted for a non-deposit lender, house precedents 2016.HK, 0998.HK, 1788.HK, 1186.HK). First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry. WHY NOT OWNER-FCF: Yixin is a hybrid, but the balance sheet is a lender's. Net finance receivables RMB32.5bn are funded by RMB32.4bn of borrowings; reported OCF swings from -8.7bn (FY2023) to +12.3bn (FY2020) purely with loan-book growth and runoff; the 'asset-light' transaction platform still carries guarantee (risk-assurance) exposure on ~RMB86bn of facilitated loans, so even the SaaS/platform side needs equity capital behind it. An EV-minus-net-debt build would subtract RMB27.7bn of book-funding debt from an EBITDA-based EV and swing the equity value from deeply negative to positive on one point of WACC, which is meaningless. A sum-of-parts (platform on owner-FCF, book on FCFE) was considered and rejected because the segment note does not allocate credit impairment, funding cost or equity between the two lines and the guarantee business straddles them; the whole-company FCFE route values the same earnings with one capital charge. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total revenues (both segments); ebitda_margin = profit before income tax PLUS share-based compensation, as % of revenue (after cost of funds, credit impairment, opex, finance cost and equity-method results); sbc_pct_path = SBC / revenue, so EBIT = PBT and the street basis = the company's adjusted net profit convention; D&A, leases and working capital zero (inside the margin); cash_tax_rate = income tax (NCI nil), so EBIT x (1 - rate) = net profit to shareholders; capex_pct_path = equity retained to hold equity/total assets at the target ratio on balance-sheet growth (target_t x assets_t - target_t-1 x assets_t-1, as % of revenue, from FY2026E total assets RMB56bn), so FCF = FCFE = distributable earnings. Terminal-decade asset growth equals terminal growth so the terminal FCFE is self-consistent. A 12x FCFE terminal cap is set for a lender (Gordon at 12% - 2.5% = 10.8x base, so it does not bind in the base; it binds nowhere). KEY FINDINGS: (1) ROE is ~8% on FY2026E (7.1% FY2025) against a 12% cost of equity, so fair value is a fraction of book (base terminal P/B ~0.6x); (2) the dividend (HK14.0 cents for FY2025, ~RMB800m, ~70% payout) is covered by FCFE of ~RMB870m only because asset growth has slowed to ~3%; the FY2025 pattern (receivables +12%, payout 68%, leverage 1.63x -> 1.85x) is not repeatable without levering further; (3) the market price (0.27x book, ~3x earnings, 18% trailing yield) sits BELOW the bear case, which implies the market is pricing a regulatory or credit event (take-rate/guarantee-fee caps, a funding-market shutout, or a Tencent-related change) that the Aug-2026 interim does not disclose; the valuation is explicitly conditional on no such event. DRIVER EVIDENCE: H1 FY2026 interim (revenue +13%; SaaS +60% to 48% of revenue; loan facilitation -48%; guarantee +22%; financing lease +6%; net take rate 6.8% vs 4.8%; net interest spread 6.0%; credit impairment +61% to RMB1,678m; PBT +7% to 847m; tax 17.0%; equity-method losses 87m; no interim dividend; 90+ day past due 1.92%); FY2025 annual (revenue +17%, PBT 1,713m, tax 30.0%, SBC 144m, dividends HK14.0 cents, borrowings 31.3bn, average funding cost 3.7%). Management gives no numeric FY2026 guidance (strategic priorities: FinTech SaaS, used-car financing, Southeast Asia). Valuation date is 9.7 months into FY2026, so FY2026E is fy0 (not discounted) and the first discounted flow is FY2027.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: medium-term revenue growth for a Chinese auto-finance platform whose SaaS line (+60%) is offset by a deliberately shrinking loan-facilitation line (-48%) and a shrinking China passenger-vehicle market (-4.4% H1 2026); base path runs 6% -> 3%. Neither the 30% revenue CAGR (recovery from the FY2020-21 trough and the FY2023-24 guarantee/SaaS launch) nor the 3% equity CAGR (ROE 2-7% on a RMB15-17bn base) is a usable forward rate.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr/5yr CAGR 3.4%/3.1% vs revenue 30.5%/28.3% and EPS 3yr 45.9% (>30% apart). Equity barely grew because FY2020-21 were a loss and near-zero years, ROE only reached 7.1% in FY2025, and ~70% of FY2025 profit was paid out. Revenue and EPS compound from a FY2020 trough (revenue 3,325, EPS -0.18) and overstate sustainable growth. Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: a lender's reported FCF (OCF - capex) is loan-book flow noise (-8,682 FY2023, +12,230 FY2020). The relevant series is net profit: 29 (FY2021) -> 371 -> 555 -> 810 -> 1,199 (FY2025) -> H1 FY2026 704 (+28%, but PBT only +7%: the H1 profit growth came from a 17% tax rate vs 31%). EPS 5yr CAGR is null because FY2020 EPS was negative (-0.184).

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +6% then fading to 3%: SaaS (48% of revenue, +60%) keeps growing but its take rate is already falling (12.3% -> 11.2%), loan facilitation (12%) keeps shrinking by design, guarantee fees (18%) track a used-car mix that regulators are squeezing, and the self-operated book grows ~4% (net interest spread 6.0%, yield 9.4%). China passenger-vehicle sales -4.4% in H1 2026 with subsidies rolling off; Southeast Asia (~US$150m H1 volume) is not yet material.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC pre-tax margin: FY2023 11.7%, FY2024 11.6%, FY2025 16.1%, H1 FY2026 15.2% (gross margin up to 64.6% from 52.9% on SaaS mix, but credit impairment +61% and equity-method losses 87m). Held ~15% then +0.5pt as AI-driven cost-to-serve gains partly offset rising credit cost on a used-car-heavy book (56% of financing volume).
base.sbc_rationale: SBC 1.24% of revenue FY2025, 1.46% H1 FY2026 (new option and award grants); glides to 1.2%.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold equity/total assets at 30% (30.5% at H1 FY2026) on total-asset growth of 4% for five years then 3% (= terminal growth), from FY2026E total assets RMB56bn (54,963 at H1 FY2026). Retention / revenue = 0.30 x g x prior assets / revenue: 5.0% in FY2027 falling to 3.7%. Terminal assets ~RMB79bn, equity ~RMB23.7bn, terminal ROE ~8.5%, terminal P/B ~0.6x.
base.tax_rationale: PRC statutory 25%: FY2025 effective 30.0% (non-deductible items, withholding), H1 FY2026 17.0% (Hainan Free Trade Port 15% preferential rate plus one-off deductions of previously unrecognised expenses, which do not repeat). 25% is the midpoint; NCI is nil.
base.terminal_note: Gordon on FY2036 FCFE at 12.0% - 2.5% = 10.8x; the 12x lender cap does not bind. Implied terminal P/B ~0.6x on ~8.5% ROE, consistent with (ROE - g)/(CoE - g).
base.narrative: Mix shift continues at a slower pace: SaaS keeps scaling, facilitation keeps shrinking, the book grows ~4%, credit cost stays high but contained; margin ~15-15.5%, FCFE RMB0.7bn rising to RMB1.3bn, dividend covered.

bull.growth_rationale: SaaS keeps compounding at 30-40% as the 'technology exporter' model lands more bank/OEM clients at stable revenue per core client, used-car financing penetration rises with the 2026 trade-in subsidy and aftermarket measures, Southeast Asia becomes material, and the 'Matthew effect' hands share to the scaled compliant leader.
bull.margin_rationale: SaaS mix lifts gross margin toward 70%, XinMM-AM1 agentic AI cuts cost-to-serve (90% of processes AI-driven), funding cost keeps falling (3.7% FY2025), credit impairment stabilises as risk controls bite; FY2025's 16.1% is the floor.
bull.capex_rationale: Equity/assets held at 30% on asset growth of 6% for three years, 5% for two, 4% for two, then 3%: faster growth costs more retained capital. Terminal assets ~RMB87bn, terminal ROE ~11%.
bull.tax_rationale: Hainan 15% preferential rate on a larger share of profit.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon 1.03/0.09 = 11.4x FCFE; cap does not bind.
bull.narrative: The SaaS pivot works: margin to 19%, revenue compounds high single digits, ROE rises to ~11%, close to the cost of equity, so the stock re-rates toward book.

bear.growth_rationale: The 2025-26 crackdown on high-interest/high-rebate auto lending and the ~24% all-in APR cap reach guarantee fees and SaaS take rates (guarantee + SaaS = 66% of revenue); facilitation keeps shrinking; new-vehicle sales fall further as subsidies roll off; the book is run flat to protect asset quality. Revenue falls ~15% over three years before stabilising.
bear.margin_rationale: Credit impairment, already +61% YoY in H1 FY2026, keeps rising on a used-car-heavy book (90+ day past-due 1.92% and climbing) while take rates are capped; margin falls through the FY2023-24 11.6% level to 8% before partly recovering to 12% as the book is repriced.
bear.capex_rationale: Funding-market stress forces deleveraging: equity/assets rebuilt from 30% to 33% over FY2027-29 on a flat balance sheet (~RMB560m/yr retained, most of a depressed profit), then held at 33% on 2% asset growth. Distributions are cut for three years. Terminal ROE ~5%.
bear.tax_rationale: Non-deductible provisions against a smaller PBT; FY2025's 30% as the reference.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon 1.02/0.10 = 10.2x FCFE; cap does not bind.
bear.narrative: Regulation caps the fee stack and credit losses keep rising; revenue falls 15%, margin halves, lenders force deleveraging, the dividend is cut; FCFE near zero for three years, terminal ROE ~5%.

scenario_narratives.base: SaaS keeps scaling while loan facilitation shrinks by design and the self-operated book grows ~4%; the pre-SBC pre-tax margin holds ~15-15.5% as AI-driven cost gains offset rising credit cost; equity/assets stays at 30% so leverage does not rise further. FCFE grows from ~RMB0.9bn (FY2026E) to ~RMB1.3bn; terminal ROE ~8.5% against a 12% cost of equity, so fair value is ~0.6x book.
scenario_narratives.bull: The 'technology exporter' pivot lands: SaaS compounds at 30-40%, used-car and Southeast Asia volumes grow, funding cost falls, credit impairment stabilises; revenue +10% fading to 3%, margin to 19%, ROE ~11%; the stock re-rates toward book value.
scenario_narratives.bear: The regulatory campaign against high-interest/high-rebate auto lending caps guarantee fees and SaaS take rates, credit losses keep rising on the used-car book, and lenders force deleveraging to 33% equity/assets. Revenue falls ~15% over three years, margin drops to 8% before recovering to 12%, distributions are cut for three years; terminal ROE ~5%. Note the current price sits below even this path, so the market is pricing something worse than modelled.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 40% (well above the 15% default): the stock has fallen ~73% from HK$2.85 in December 2025 to a 52-week low, with a 100m-share volume spike on 13-15 October 2026, and nothing in the August 2026 interim explains it, so the market is signalling an event (regulatory take-rate/guarantee-fee cap, funding-market shutout, credit deterioration, or a Tencent-related change) that the filings do not yet show; credit impairment rose 61% YoY in H1 FY2026 with PBT up only 7%; 66% of revenue (guarantee + SaaS) is exposed to the 2025-26 crackdown on high-rebate auto lending; funding is wholesale-only. Bull 15%: needs SaaS scaling, credit stabilisation and regulatory calm simultaneously, in a shrinking vehicle market. Base 45%: H1 FY2026 operating results (revenue +13%, net take rate 6.8%, spread 6.0%, dividend covered) are consistent with the base path.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Yixin is valued as a lender, not as a SaaS company: the self-operated financing-lease book is funded 1:1 by wholesale borrowings, the 'asset-light' platform retains guarantee exposure on ~RMB86bn of facilitated loans, and reported free cash flow is loan-book noise. The flow that belongs to shareholders is net profit less the equity that must be retained to hold leverage flat as the balance sheet grows (FCFE), discounted at a CNY cost of equity of 12% with net debt zero by construction. The Group earns ~7-8% on equity against that 12%, so it is fairly worth well under book even in the base case (~0.6x). The share price (0.27x book, ~3x earnings, 18% trailing yield) is below the bear case, which means the market is pricing an event the filings do not disclose; the valuation is conditional on no such event and the bear weight is set at 40% to reflect that uncertainty. SBC is expensed in the flows and the fully diluted count is held flat; the street basis (SBC added back) equals the company's 'adjusted net profit' convention.
valuation_philosophy.model_choice: Routed via dcf-methods: 'Bank, non-bank deposit taker, thrift' adapted for a non-deposit lender, implemented as FCFE at cost of equity on the engine route (house precedents 2016.HK, 0998.HK, 1788.HK, 1186.HK). Owner-FCF with EV minus RMB27.7bn of book-funding net debt was rejected as meaningless; a platform/book sum-of-parts was rejected because the segment note does not allocate credit cost, funding cost or equity between the two lines and the guarantee business straddles them.
key_risks_to_valuation: Unexplained ~73% share-price drawdown in 2026 with a mid-October volume spike: if it reflects a regulatory cap on guarantee fees/take rates or a funding event, the bear path is too mild.

Credit: impairment +61% YoY in H1 FY2026 to RMB1,678m, 90+ day past-due 1.92% and rising on a book that is 56% used-car; guarantee exposure on ~RMB86bn of off-balance-sheet loans with RMB2.87bn of provisions.
Regulation: 2025-26 provincial bans on high-interest/high-rebate auto loans and the ~24% all-in APR cap reach exactly the fee stack (guarantee + SaaS = 66% of revenue) that drives the margin.
Funding: wholesale-only (ABS, syndicated loans, USD bond, MTNs) against 1.93x debt-to-equity; a shutout forces deleveraging that consumes FCFE, as in the bear case.
Earnings quality: H1 FY2026 net profit +28% on a 17% tax rate (Hainan preferential rate and one-off deductions) while PBT grew 7%; the model uses 25%.

Concentration and control: 24 core customers are 99% of SaaS revenue; Tencent holds ~52%, so minority holders have no say on capital allocation; 10% PRC dividend withholding for H-share holders is not modelled.
Currency and listing: RMB flows against an HKD quote (a 10% RMB move is a 10% move in HKD value).
